deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform may delete the playbook, abandon it from Terraform management, or prevent its destruction. A policy should require PREVENT to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorised deletion disrupting the agent's generative conversation workflow.

display_name.description: The human-readable name of the playbook, unique within an agent.
display_name.rationale: Sets the human-readable name used to identify the playbook. Although the name may be visible to the LLM, a generic name-pattern policy cannot determine whether its content is safe; it is descriptive metadata rather than an authentication, authorisation, data-protection or execution control.

goal.description: High level description of the goal the playbook intend to accomplish. A goal should be concise since it's visible to other playbooks that may reference this playbook.
goal.rationale: Defines the application-specific objective supplied to the LLM. Unsafe text is possible, but string matching cannot reliably determine semantic prompt safety or the correct goal without understanding the intended workflow, so it is not a meaningful generic platform-policy target.

parent.description:
The agent to create a Playbook for.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>.
parent.rationale: Identifies the Dialogflow CX agent that owns the playbook. It is a team-specific resource reference, and constraining it would require pinning a particular project, location or agent; resource placement and access should instead be governed through organisation controls and IAM.

playbook_type.description: Type of the playbook. Possible values: ["PLAYBOOK_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "TASK", "ROUTINE"]
playbook_type.rationale: Selects TASK or ROUTINE behaviour, with the unspecified value defaulting to TASK. Neither supported type represents elevated privilege or administrative access, so this is a functional architecture choice rather than a generic security control.

referenced_tools.description: The resource name of tools referenced by the current playbook in the instructions. If not provided explicitly, they are will be implied using the tool being referenced in goal and steps.
referenced_tools.rationale: Lists the resource names of tools referenced by the playbook. The permitted tools depend on the application, and constraining this list would pin team-specific identifiers; tool capabilities and access should be secured on the referenced tools and through IAM.

instruction.guidelines.description: General guidelines for the playbook. These are unstructured instructions that are not directly part of the goal, e.g. "Always be polite". It's valid for this text to be long and used instead of steps altogether.
instruction.guidelines.rationale: Defines unstructured, application-specific guidance for the LLM. Unsafe content is possible, but a generic string rule cannot reliably identify prompt injection or determine correct guidance without workflow context, so this requires design review and runtime safeguards rather than a uniform value constraint.

instruction.steps.description: Ordered list of step by step execution instructions to accomplish target goal.

instruction.steps.steps.description:
Sub-processing needed to execute the current step.

This field uses JSON data as a string. The value provided must be a valid JSON representation documented in [Step](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents.playbooks#step).
instruction.steps.steps.rationale: Encodes application-specific nested playbook steps as JSON. The provider validates the document structure, while safe sequencing and tool use depend on the surrounding workflow; a generic value policy cannot reliably infer recursion or unauthorised execution paths from arbitrary step content.

instruction.steps.text.rationale: Defines the natural-language instruction for an individual playbook step. Its required content depends on the intended task and cannot be validated for security using a generic value constraint.

llm_model_settings.description: Llm model settings for the playbook.

llm_model_settings.model.rationale: Selects a supported LLM model. Model availability and suitability evolve and depend on workload requirements; the model identifier alone does not represent a universally insecure configuration.

llm_model_settings.prompt_text.rationale: Defines a custom, application-specific prompt for the selected model. Unsafe prompt content is possible, but semantic prompt safety cannot be reliably enforced through a generic string-value policy without understanding the intended workflow.
